x: Rathbone came along next, walking quite comfortably and with lots of strength in hand. Manning and Wattam pleased the crowd, as also did Bidgood. Fletcher came along in the last group, smiling and determined.
Hillier was tenth, and our others, Khlopin, Holman and Wattam—once again making his annual journey from Lincolnshire for the race—were further back, taking things steadily.

Wattam, the last-named once again making the journey from his Lincolnshire home to try conclusions with the Brighton road. At the first stopping point on the road, “The Swan and Sugar Loaf,” at South Croydon, about 10½ miles, our ’bus load of supporters were all smiles, for we had three men in the first group of four.

A word of praise to our lesser lights: Allen, Bicknell, Yorwarth, Laurie, Spooner, Wattam and Willis for their efforts. Also, many thanks to the willing band of cyclists who did yeoman work as attendants.
